hook_text: On 31 May 1910 a new country was born. About one in five people were white, but they held almost all the power.
clip_script: Gold made the Transvaal the richest prize in Africa. In 1899 Britain went to war with the Boer republics to get it. Farms burned, and thousands died in camps, Boer and black. In 1902 the peace came, with one quiet clause: the vote for black people would wait. People who were left out organised. Coloured leaders formed the APO. Indians in the Transvaal formed their own congress and learned to refuse unfair laws peacefully. In Natal, Bambatha rose against a new tax, and machine guns crushed the rebellion. Then in 1910, four colonies became one: the Union of South Africa. Peace between Boer and Briton. Exclusion for almost everyone else.
visual_style: A whiteboard timeline from 1899 to 1910, with a gold nugget, a peace treaty, three organisation badges, a broken spear for Bambatha and a parliament building filled with one colour.
pacing: Brisk through the war, slowing at the 1910 reveal.
